items.title: Tommy Ridgley Interview, 1986-06-20
items.q: To do that Ray Charles, the old Ray Charles...

ctx.x: St. Augustine Hall with Marcel Richardson. Oh, yeah? Oh, yeah? David Black, David on sax. Oh, yeah. Oh, yeah. Oh, yeah. And they killed him. They killed him. Wait, did he do his Ray Charles? Yeah, he did some couple of Ray Charles.
Of course, we always killed him. He's the last man I know other than Snook Elgin, but he was always better than Snook Elgin. To do that Ray Charles, the old Ray Charles. And that's so cool.
Yeah, right. He reminded me of that.

items.title: Tommy Ridgley Interview, 1986-04-23
items.q: And when they came in to record me, well, Ray Charles did. He was, he's the producer. He produced the record. And I remember Jerry Wexler told Ray Charles to play, but don't play like Ray Charles.

ctx.x: I thought you had a pretty good piano player. Okay. Okay. Okay, yeah. Now you see that ring the bell. Okay. Now, now, now, I can remember. Okay. Ray Charles was in town. Ray Charles was in town because he stayed around New Orleans quite a bit because he wasn't the superstar like he is now. And he would live at Foster's down the street from the Dew Drop, but he was hanging in the Dew Drop. And Atlantic came in town and Ray Charles was having these records with Atlantic. And when they came in to record me, well,…
I think that was the song we haven't told you.

items.title: Tommy Ridgley Interview, 1986-03-22
items.q: I remember at the Dewdrop, me, Willie John, Ray Charles. Oh, me, Willie John, Ray Charles. And they had somebody else. But they had one other big star. We had like a grand finale on the bandstand at the Dewdrop.

ctx.x: Okay, we talked about, you mentioned the Blue Eagle. Blue Eagle. Okay. Was that a rougher club than say?

Yes, sir. When you say the Blue Eagle, you say it's a rough neighborhood, rough club, rough people, used to come into Blue Eagle. You would guarantee on a dance night at the Blue Eagle, guarantee a fight. It was like automatic. You know somebody was going to get their head bust or something. You know, it wasn't that much killing back then. But they would fight. Somebody might get, occasionally you would hear somebody would get shot or something like that. But it's very occasional. But, you know, like I always…
Were there any problems with whites going to the Dewdrop?
